title: How H&M Really Makes Money (Without Owning a Single Factory)
description:
H&M sold clothes worth about SEK 228 billion (around $24 billion) in 2025, yet it doesn't own a single factory. In this file we open the money machine behind H&M: a women's shop called Hennes in Västerås, a hunting store that gave the company its menswear and its name, hundreds of supplier factories, where every SEK 100 of sales goes, designer collaborations, COS, ARKET and Sellpy, and why the Persson family now owns about 69% of the company.

{CHAPTERS}

Sources: H&M Group full-year report 2025 (January 2026); H&M Group nine-month report 2026 (September 2026); H&M Group Annual and Sustainability Report 2025 press release; H&M Group history, About us and supply chain pages; Shenglu Lu / FASH455 analysis of H&M's supplier list (2026); South China Morning Post (H&M history); Apparel Insider; Billionaires.Africa and Texture (Persson family stake, 2026).

All figures are rounded; "per SEK 100" figures are our own arithmetic from reported numbers, and the dollar figure is an approximate conversion. This video is for education only, not investment advice.
